I wrote the migrated file to `out/module.ts`, and all three lodash imports are gone. I did not check its results against the original, because `lodash` isn't installed, so the original won't build.

**Installed es-toolkit is 1.53.2.** I read the declarations of the functions below in that package.

| lodash call | replacement |
|---|---|
| `pick(row, ['id','name'])` | `pick` from `es-toolkit`, which has the same call shape. |
| `sumBy(rows, 'age')` | `sumBy` from `es-toolkit`, called as `sumBy(rows, r => r.age)`. The main entry only accepts a callback; the string shorthand exists only in `es-toolkit/compat`. |
| `fromPairs(pairs)` | `zipObject(pairs.map(p => p[0]), pairs.map(p => p[1]))` from `es-toolkit`. `fromPairs` exists only in `es-toolkit/compat`, so I used `zipObject` with a one-line adapter that splits the pairs into keys and values. With repeated names, the last value wins, as before. |

I kept the exported signatures and types unchanged, so no lodash import remains.

**Checks**
- **Bundle size:** `npm run size -- out/module.ts` reports 244 bytes (min+gzip) and 129 bytes of own code. I couldn't get the original's figures to compare, since its build fails on the missing `lodash`. I also didn't measure the `es-toolkit/compat` `fromPairs` alternative.
- **Type check:** `npx tsc --noEmit` reports no errors for `out/module.ts`. Its only errors are the missing `lodash` modules in `src/module.ts`.
